02 · The threat

Jamming comes from
the horizon.

One ground jammer can silence every satellite at once.

Satellite signals travel ~20,000 km and arrive below the noise floor. A nearby jammer at 0–15° elevation easily overpowers them across all GNSS bands.

03 · LEANA

Deaf to the horizon.
Sharp at the sky.

Signals from low angles are turned down 100×.

Low Elevation Angle Nulling Antenna: 20 dB (typ.) wideband suppression from 0° to ~15° elevation, all GNSS bands. Above 20°: excellent gain and a stable phase centre.

04 · Stand-off distance

Up to 10× closer
to a jammer.

Demonstrated with a jammer at 10° elevation, compared with a standard HC977XF helical antenna.

−20 dB = 1/100 of the jamming power
Power ∝ 1/distance² → √100 = 10×
05 · XF+ eXtended Filtering

Noise in. Clean signal out.

> 80 dB out-of-band rejection, 700–2500 MHz

Deep filtering and high linearity knock down LTE, Ligado and Inmarsat signals before they reach the receiver.

06 · Split channels

Two channels.
Twice the resilience.

XF+ separates the LNA's upper and lower amplification channels. If one is jammed, the other stays usable.

01 · Four elements

Four elements.
One sense of direction.

Quad-element, dual-feed stacked patch array (Tallysman Accutenna®). Small arrival-time differences between elements reveal where each signal comes from.

02 · Null steering

Finds the jammer.
Goes deaf to it.

Adaptive null forming steers a deep notch in the reception pattern toward the interference, in real time, while satellites stay in view.

03 · Multiple threats

Up to three jammers.
At once.

Full-band GNSS antenna

TW7990XF

Every signal.
Precision you can trust.
Full band + L-bandAccutenna®XF filtering32 dB LNA
01 · Coverage

Full band.
Every constellation.

02 · Inside

Two feeds.
One clean signal.

Dual-feed stacked RHCP ceramic patch with orthogonal feeds, combined in a hybrid, amplified by a wideband LNA, split for narrow filtering and recombined.

03 · Multipath

Ignores
the echoes.

Reflections flip polarization (RHCP → LHCP). Circular polarization purity rejects them for superior multipath rejection.

04 · Precision

Rock-steady
phase centre.

Low axial ratio (< 2 dB at zenith) and tight phase centre variation, for full-band RTK and PPP.

05 · XF eXtended Filtering

Noise in. Clean signal out.

Calian custom XF filtering

Mitigates existing interference plus new Ligado and LTE signals, and protects against intermodulation and saturation from strong 700 MHz LTE.

06 · Applications

Built for machines
that move.

Autonomous vehicle and robot guidance, PTC / PTL rail, precision agriculture, full-band RTK and PPP, law enforcement and public safety.

The first full-size smart choke ring

VCS6000XF

A reference station
in one antenna.
Full band + L-bandSeptentrio mosaic-X50.5 mm PCVPoE · IP67
01 · Coverage

Every
constellation.

02 · Receiver inside

Antenna and receiver.
One unit.

A geodetic VeraChoke element wired straight into a Septentrio receiver. A short RF chain means low noise.

All-in-view 448-channel mosaic-X5 · up to 100 Hz · OSNMA · 32 GB logging · repeatable RF performance unit to unit.

03 · Multipath

Echoes get
trapped.

The 3D choke ring catches signals bouncing off the ground and nearby walls before they reach the element. APME+ in the receiver cleans up what's left.

04 · Phase centre

0.5 mm
phase centre.

The point it measures from barely moves, whichever way the satellite comes from.

Precise PCO, 0.5 mm PCV, GEO++ calibration. Axial ratio L1 < 0.2 dB, full band < 0.3 dB, zenith to horizon. Minimizes RTK network biases.

05 · GNSS+ protection

Built-in
defences.

Septentrio's GNSS+ technologies watch every signal for jamming, spoofing and other trouble.

06 · Base station

Plug in.
Corrections out.

Connect over PoE Ethernet or USB, with no rack or separate receiver. The built-in NTRIP caster streams RTK corrections to rovers.

M12(X) to RJ45 · low-cost CAT5e · 20 m marine-grade cable included (longer options) · RTCM 3 (MSM) · CMR · RINEX · NMEA · SBF · USB setup.

07 · Robots

Ring off.
Ready to roll.

Take the choke ring off and fit two on a robot, one at the front and one at the back. With NTRIP corrections from a base station, it knows exactly where it is and which way it's facing.

Two antennas: position + heading · 3 mm horizontal / 8 mm vertical static (2σ) · up to 100 Hz · PoE or USB.

08 · Surveying

Survey poles
and structures.

On a survey pole it measures points around bridges, roads and buildings, using corrections streamed from a second unit at the base station.

One VCS6000XF as the NTRIP base station, one on the pole. Each point is recorded with RTK precision.
